prompt:
You check whether a student's answer shows one way of understanding a Java concept.

Program:
int i, n = 5;
for (i = 1; i < n; i++)
    i++;
    System.out.println(i);
System.out.println(i);

Question: Without tracing line by line, explain what this code does for any value of n.

Student's answer, split into clauses:
c1: Whatever n is, i starts at 1 and goes up by 2 on every pass
c2: so the loop stops at the first odd number that is n or more
c3: The program prints that number twice
c4: For n = 5 that is 5
c5: for n = 6 it would be 7

Concept: loop_body
Way: one step execution
What an answer that shows this way does: One pass of the body changes exactly the variables it assigns (e.g. print i and v, double v, increment i) and these changes carry into the next test and pass.

Decide:
- shown: the answer does what this way describes, in its own words or in code (states that rule, traces it, predicts it, relates it, applies it);
- not shown: the answer does not do this.

Reply in exactly three lines and nothing else:
Label: shown | not shown
Clauses: the numbers of the clauses that show it, e.g. 2, 4 (write none if not shown)
Confidence: a number from 0 to 1
